title: Ray diagrams for a converging lens
caption: A lens with f = 10 cm. Use the ray rules: a ray parallel to the axis passes through F; a ray through the centre is undeviated; a ray through F emerges parallel. Where they meet is the image. At 2F the image is real, inverted and the same size; inside F the rays diverge and only appear to come from a virtual, upright, magnified image.
alt: Three ray diagrams for a converging lens of focal length 10 cm: object beyond 2F, object at 2F, and object inside F.
description: Each panel shows the principal axis, a converging lens drawn as a vertical double-headed arrow, and the focal points F and 2F on both sides. The lens has focal length 10 cm.
Object beyond 2F (30 cm away): the rays meet 15 cm beyond the lens, forming a real, inverted, diminished image.
Object at 2F (20 cm away): the rays meet at 2F on the other side, forming a real, inverted image the same size as the object.

Object inside F (6 cm away): the rays spread out after the lens. Traced backwards (dashed), they meet 15 cm in front of the lens on the object's side, forming a virtual, upright image 2.5 times larger. This is a magnifying glass.

review.notes: Round 1: label overlaps; caption did not give f; fixed. Round 2: remaining label offsets fixed.
